failure_definition: Pulse oximeter inaccuracy in low perfusion conditions, resulting in unreliable SpO₂ estimates.
causal_mechanism: Low perfusion reduces the signal-to-noise ratio of the photoplethysmographic (PPG) waveform, degrading its quality and making it difficult to distinguish arterial blood from venous blood and other tissue components.
current_device_behavior: Traditional two-wavelength (red and infrared) pulse oximeters provide SpO₂ estimates based on the ratio of light absorption by oxygenated and deoxygenated hemoglobin.
failure_point: The calibration algorithm of the pulse oximeter fails to accurately account for low perfusion conditions, leading to inaccuracy in SpO₂ estimates.
blocking_constraint: The need for a controlled study to validate the effectiveness of the proposed modification, incorporating a third wavelength, in improving the accuracy of pulse oximeter readings in low perfusion conditions.
